summary: A 1936 CCC-built 31 ft Aermotor tower on Hutch Mountain, Coconino NF, registered 2006; staffing rests on a 2018 blog and undated listings.

facts.design: 31 ft Aermotor MC-24 tower with a 12 x 12 ft wooden R-3 cab; built without a catwalk, steel catwalk added 2008

access.note: The road is typically open from late spring to autumn and closed in winter; climbing is by permission of the lookout on duty

visit.trail_note: Forest Road 135 from Forest Highway 3 (Lake Mary Road), then Forest Road 135B; a Forest Service gate sits around mile 4 and the lookout is about a quarter-mile past it

events.note: September 1935 memos propose replacing the Mahan tower with a 30 ft tower on Hutch Mountain, to be erected with CCC labor
CCC built the present tower, replacing a wooden tower from the 1920s
Steel catwalk added in the fall

evidence.supports: early-1920s wooden tower on the Mogollon Rim District of Coconino NF
evidence.quote: The original lookout at Hutch Mountain on the Mogollon Rim District of the Coconino National Forest was a wooden tower built in the early 1920s.

evidence.supports: 1936 CCC built the present 31 ft Aermotor MC-24 tower with a 12 x 12 wooden R-3 cab without catwalk
evidence.quote: In 1936 the CCC built the present 31' Aermotor MC-24 tower with a live in 12'x12' wooden R-3 cab without catwalk.

evidence.supports: September 1935 proposal to replace the Mahan tower with a tower on Hutch Mountain
evidence.quote: The tower on Mahan is in fairly good condition but if possible I would like to replace it with a tower on Hutch Mountain.

evidence.supports: Hutch is higher and covers the country Mahan sees
evidence.quote: Hutch Mountain is a higher point and covers all of the country which Mahan sees

evidence.supports: a later memo: a 30 ft structure would be ample
evidence.quote: I have looked into the matter of new towers for Bakers Butte and Hutch Mountain and found that the 30-ft. structure at either place would be ample to cover the fire country.
2008: In the fall a steel catwalk was added.

evidence.supports: southeast of Flagstaff, Coconino National Forest
evidence.quote: go southeast of town and head up the Coconino National Forest’s Hutch Mountain

evidence.supports: lookout on duty will likely give permission to climb; tower built by CCC in 1936 to replace a 1920s wooden tower
evidence.quote: he or she likely will give you permission to climb the tower, which was built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1936 to replace a wooden tower erected in the 1920s.

evidence.supports: Forest Road 135 rocky and rutted but suitable for most SUVs
evidence.quote: From the paved highway, head east on Forest Road 135, which is rocky and rutted but suitable for most SUVs.

evidence.supports: route turns onto Forest Road 135B up Hutch Mountain
evidence.quote: FR 135 then climbs into a thick stand of ponderosas before you turn left onto Forest Road 135B, the route up Hutch Mountain.

evidence.supports: Forest Service gate around mile 4; lookout about a quarter-mile past it
evidence.quote: The Hutch Mountain Lookout is about a quarter-mile past this gate.

evidence.supports: Forest Road 135B off Lake Mary Road, also Forest Highway 3
evidence.quote: Starting directly off Lake Mary Road, also known as Forest Highway 3

evidence.supports: road typically open late spring to autumn; closed in winter
evidence.quote: The road is typically open from late spring to autumn but remains closed in winter due to snow accumulation.

evidence.supports: listing calls the tower historic and active
evidence.quote: At the summit, the historic and active Hutch Mountain fire lookout tower serves as the main highlight

evidence.supports: 2018 blog: tower still a manned viewpoint for fires in the Flagstaff area
evidence.quote: It was built in 1936, and still serves as a manned major viewpoint for fires in the Flagstaff area.

evidence.supports: Hutch Mountain tower standing, NHLR US 676
evidence.quote: Hutch Mountain Coconino 34.80194 -111.39017 Tower Standing NHLR US 676, AZ 63

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1935 memos planned a 30 ft tower; the NHLR describes the 1936 tower as 31 ft. I used 31 ft as the as-built figure (9.4 m), since the register describes what was erected.

notes_for_editor: Current staffing rests on a 2018 personal blog and on undated Arizona Highways and onX listings, none from the Forest Service; verify with the Coconino National Forest before publishing staffing as current. The Forest Service Coconino recreation page was readable but did not mention Hutch Mountain. Climbing is described as by permission of the lookout on duty only; the story says not to climb without it. The Arizona Highways article and the onX listing are undated in the pages read. An undated memo from a Long Valley district ranger, describing the earlier cabin as a substandard 10 by 10 ft, appears on the westlookouts page and was not used. The 31 ft figure may be the tower height or the overall structure; I read it as tower height for height_m. No new photos checked. The westlookouts page's 1936 entry says a 30 ft MC-24 replaced the lookout at Mahan Mountain, which conflicts with the NHLR's 1936 31 ft MC-24 at Hutch; the story follows the NHLR for Hutch and does not mention the Mahan entry.
